title: Mark: The Suffering King
speaker: Ger Jones
notes: Pastor Ger explores what it means to share the love of Jesus in a way that is authentic, relational, and rooted in grace. Through Genesis 12 and stories from the life of Jesus, Ger reminds us that we are blessed to be a blessing—and that evangelism doesn’t have to be complicated or intimidating. Instead, we can create safe spaces for people to explore faith, live with compelling curiosity, love people well, and simply play our part while trusting God with the rest. This message offers a fresh vision for sharing our faith, inviting us to reflect the love of Jesus and help others discover Him for themselves.

title: Explore Jesus for Yourself
speaker: Ger Jones
notes: Pastor Ger Jones invites us to explore one of life’s biggest questions: Who is Jesus? Through the story of Nathaniel in John 1 and his own journey from skepticism to faith, Pastor Ger explores what it means to honestly investigate Jesus, wrestle with doubt, and ask the questions that matter most. From searching for meaning in career, success, and pleasure to discovering the love and life found in Jesus, this message is an invitation to come and see for yourself. You don’t have to take a blind leap of faith—you can explore Jesus, ask the hard questions, and discover who He really is.

title: The Love You Had at First
speaker: Kristen Maynard
notes: Pastor Kristen Maynard delivers an insightful teaching on Revelation 2, focusing on the church in Ephesus and the critical call to return to "the love you had at first". She explores the challenge of maintaining deep, unreserved devotion to God amidst the busyness and demands of life, cautioning against allowing routine service to replace a genuine, heart-centered relationship with Jesus. This message serves as a powerful reminder to prioritize intimacy with God above mere outward performance, encouraging a season of reflection and renewed passion in our walk with Him.

title: The Church Origin Story Pt. 3
speaker: Ger Jones
notes: Pastor Ger continues our series in Acts, looking at the early church and what it means to be the family of God. Through Acts 2, we see a community shaped by the Holy Spirit, marked by togetherness, generosity, belonging, and a shared life. In a city like Los Angeles, where individualism and busyness can easily pull us apart, what would it look like to intentionally choose life together? Ger explores how the Holy Spirit forms us into a people, why we need both the big and the small, and how we can embrace the messy reality of becoming a community where everyone is known, loved, and belongs.

title: The Church Origin Story Pt. 2
speaker: Ger Jones
notes: Pastor Ger Jones continues our series in Acts as we look at the birth of the early church and the coming of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost. As we ask what it means to be the church, we’re reminded that the church is a people empowered by the Holy Spirit to live out the mission Jesus has given us. Ger explores what it looks like to depend on the Spirit, live with boldness, and be part of what God is doing in the world.

title: The Church Origin Story Pt. 1
speaker: Ger Jones
notes: Pastor Ger Jones kicks off our new series in Acts, inviting us to step into the story of the early church and discover what happens when ordinary people are empowered by the Holy Spirit. The book of Acts isn’t just a story about what God did then. It’s an invitation to ask what He might want to do through His church today.

title: The God of Mercy and Judgement
speaker: Dr. Esau McCaulley
notes: Guest speaker Esau McCaulley returns for part two of his teaching through Jonah and Nahum, exploring what these books reveal about God’s mercy, justice, and power. Looking at Nahum 1, Esau unpacks the tension between God’s judgment and His goodness, reminding us that God is both a refuge for those who trust Him and a God who confronts evil and oppression. As we live between Jonah and Nahum, we’re invited to trust the God who is merciful, just, and ultimately committed to rescuing His people.

title: Jonah 4:1-11
speaker: Dr. Esau McCaulley
notes: Guest speaker Dr. Esau McCaulley joins us at our Santa Monica location for a powerful message from Jonah, inviting us to consider what it looks like to follow God even when it's difficult. Through Jonah's story, Esau challenged us to trust God's leading, receive His grace, and extend that same grace to others—even those we may struggle to love. Ultimately, we're reminded that the relentless love of God is never meant to be kept to ourselves, but shared with the world.
